Subject: Re: FintechCo discovery — API auth & key management (post-call recap)

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the auth/key management requirements for the integration: 

What we heard you need:
- Server-to-server integration for document ingestion + embeddings and a separate pipeline for reranking (internal only).
- Prefer short-lived tokens (JWT/OAuth2 client_credentials) over long-lived API keys; but need a fallback for legacy systems.
- Service accounts per-environment (prod/stage) with role-based scopes and IP allow-listing.
- Key rotation policy: target 90-day rotation for keys, but you asked about automated rotation and KMS/HSM integration.
- Audit logs and exportable usage by key for procurement/security review.

What Redwood will deliver / next steps:
1) Docs: I attached a short questionnaire (fintechco_authn_qs.pdf) — can you fill the highlighted fields for your preferred flows? I also attached our Redwood Integration Guide (redwood-integration-guide-v1.2.pdf) and a SOC2 summary (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf).
2) Recommended auth pattern: server-side service account + OAuth2 client_credentials issuing short-lived JWTs; sign with a customer-managed KMS key if you require HSM-backed signing. We can also support API keys scoped to routes and rate limits for legacy systems.
3) Examples: we'll share sample token exchange calls and SDK snippets for both node/python server flows and a client-side approach if needed.
4) Security scoping call: propose Wed May 16 at 09:00 PT or 11:00 PT — please let us know which works. We'll bring our security engineer (Aditya) and solutions lead (Neha).
5) Sandbox POC: Neha can provision a sandbox org and pre-create a service account so you can test embedding/reranker calls with short-lived tokens.

Open questions for you (please reply inline):
- Do you have an existing KMS provider you prefer (GCP KMS, AWS KMS/HSM, or vendor-managed)?
- Are you able to accept OAuth2 client_credentials for your ingestion pipeline, or do you require static API keys?
- Any compliance checklist items we should surface prior to the security call?

Action items assigned:
- Samir / Elena: complete fintechco_authn_qs.pdf and confirm preferred call time.
- Neha: prepare sample client_credentials flow and sandbox credentials.
- Aditya: prepare notes on KMS integration options and audit log export.

Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this is great and matches what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- For KMS: we run on AWS and would prefer AWS KMS with HSM for signing if possible.
- Client_credentials looks good for the ingestion job, but we do have a few legacy systems that would prefer static API keys for the near term. Ideally we want an automated rotation system for those.
- Can you share a short example of the JWT exchange and recommended TTLs? We typically prefer TTLs <= 30 minutes for tokens, and rotation windows for signing keys every 90 days.
- SOC2 evidence: can you confirm format and whether you can provide a letter or a compressed package?

Wed May 16 11:00 PT works for us. Thanks for looping in Aditya and Neha.

—Samir

Samir —

Thanks — confirming Wed May 16 11:00 PT on our calendars. Quick answers inline to your questions: 

- AWS KMS: yes, we support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS for signing and envelope encryption. We'll document the steps for delegating a signing key and using it for token issuance.
- JWT TTLs: we recommend access tokens with TTLs between 5 and 30 minutes depending on sensitivity; refresh-style flows are used for longer sessions. For server-to-server client_credentials flows, 15 minutes is a common default at Redwood.
- API keys: we can support scoped API keys with route-level limits and automated rotation via our key management API. For legacy systems, we recommend short-lived API keys (rotate every 30–90 days) and automated rotation scripts that call the Redwood Key Management endpoint.
- SOC2: attaching a redwood_soc2_summary.pdf now; for a formal package we can provide a compressed evidence bundle via a secure share (or sign an NDA if required).

I've attached a short sample flow in the Integration Guide for client_credentials and a reference to our SDKs. Neha — can you prepare the sample client_credentials exchange (node/python) and a one-page checklist for the security call?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi all —

Following up with a few technical notes that will help scope the POC and security call: 

- Recommended pattern: OAuth2 client_credentials + JWTs signed by either Redwood (default) or your AWS KMS key. We can validate via JWKS and rotate signing keys without downtime if you use standard kid headers.
- Token TTLs: server-to-server 15m default; ingestion batch workers that need longer-lived tokens can use short-lived refresh tokens issued by a trusted exchange (we'll show the pattern).
- API keys: we support per-route scopes (embeddings vs generation vs admin) and rate limits; keys can be associated with service accounts and have rotation endpoints.
- Audit logs: we expose token/key-level usage logs in the Console and as exports to S3 (CSV/JSON) for SIEM ingest.
- Embeddings/reranker notes: include model names in request headers (x-redwood-model) and we recommend separate keys for embedding writers vs reranker readers to limit blast radius.

Sandbox offer: once we get the questionnaire back, I can create a sandbox org and pre-provision a service account with a sample client_id/client_secret for you to test the client_credentials flow. If FintechCo wants AWS KMS signing, we'll provide the steps to upload a public key or configure trust.

I'll prepare the sample node/python snippets and drop them in the Drive link before the call.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
